name: Proximity sensor
plain: Android reads the distance; iOS gives only a near or far boolean.
meaning: Shows the phone is at the ear or in a pocket. Low value as an ID.

android.note: Often binary (0 or 5 cm), some devices return distance

limits.headline: Can tell if something is close to the screen, such as your ear
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when you hold the phone to your ear on a call or voice message
can: Check if the phone is near your face
Turn off the screen during calls
On some Android phones, get a distance in centimeters
cannot: Get a distance on iPhone; only near or far
See what is near the phone
limits.differs: iPhone gives only near or far. Android is often near or far but some phones give a distance.

story.what_it_is: An app can sense when something, like your face, is close to the top of the phone.

marketing.name: Proximity sensor
marketing.pitch: Apple lets apps know when the phone is near your face so the screen can turn off during calls.

marketing.name: Position sensors
marketing.pitch: Android apps can read how close an object is to the screen to run call features.

story.for_you: You notice it only during calls: when the phone touches your ear, the screen goes dark so your cheek cannot hang up. It can also tell that the phone is in your pocket.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to switch off the screen during voice calls and voice notes. It has little value for tracking, except to guess that a phone is in a pocket or bag.

use_cases.example: A chat app turns the screen off when you hold the phone to your ear to hear a voice note.
A video call app turns the screen off during an audio only call.
A hands free app uses a wave over the sensor to answer or silence a call.
A gesture game lets you wave a hand over the phone to trigger an action.
A phone tracker app guesses that the phone is in a pocket to decide whether to ring louder.
A sleep tracker pauses buzzing when the phone is covered under a pillow.

story.android_note: Android apps can read a distance value, though many phones only give near or far.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps only get a near or far yes or no, and must turn it on first.
